summary: GAP-183 holds (5/5 real reuse hits, 2-hop chains, real non-dry GC). The narrow fix-3 changes are correct in themselves: viaMarker tagging cannot be forged (6 alias forms + a junction all collapse to the trusted entry), and the pass-1 gate is the only action-producing branch for scanned sessions. But neither STRUCTURAL claim holds for the class. (1) GAP-189 class: pass 2 still uses command-line marker TEXT to authorize deletion. A plain node process with --sutradhar-launch plus a dead owner can point --user-data-dir at ANY victim dir, which gets deleted as orphan-browser. That path skips the 120s grace and also bypasses D2 Puppeteer attribution. Live-reproduced: a ~1s-old sutradhar-cli dir and an unowned foreign puppeteer dir were both deleted, and the controls were kept. fix-3's own f3-gap189-final-confirm.json shows this same effect (carrier's 1s-old dir deleted), while fix-3-summary.md claims '0 real actions ... carrier dir still exist'. (2) GAP-188 class: 'unreadable' is unified at scan level, but it only protects a browser downstream through the --sutradhar-state marker link. A legacy (pre-0.5.0, unmarked) CLI Chrome whose state.json is locked or garbled is killed as legacy-orphan and its profile deleted. Live-reproduced with a real, reachable Chrome: exit 0, with the state file reported as 'unreadable-state' kept.
